 close Video John Daly: Finishing 2nd to Tiger & Losing $1.65M in Vegas | Hang Out with Sean Hannity 
 Golf icon John Daly joins Sean Hannity for his most raw interview yet—opening up about losing $1.65 million in a single Vegas trip after finishing second to Tiger Woods and how his wife Ana saved his life. 
In this deeply personal and hilarious episode of Hang Out with Sean Hannity, two-time major champion John Daly pulls back the curtain on his legendary "Grip It and Rip It" career and the turbulent personal battles behind the scenes. From racking up over $100,000 in PGA Tour fines and hitting golf balls off a Coors Light can with Kid Rock, to the brutal custody battle for his son Little John and quitting whiskey for good, Daly holds nothing back. Later in the episode, John’s wife of 20 years, Ana, joins the conversation to share the untold story of how they pulled each other out of dark times, the truth about his current relationship with gambling and alcohol, and their shared Christian faith.
 Dan Hicks, the beloved sports broadcaster known for his time covering golf and the Olympics, died of a lung infection, according to his death certificate.
 The California Post obtained the certificate, which stated Hicks’ tragic death was caused by multifocal pneumonia.
 Hicks was pronounced dead at 5:32 p.m. on Nov. 11 in Greenwich, Conn. He was 64 years old.
 CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE 
 NBC broadcasters Dan Hicks (left) and Johnny Miller speak during a press conference about Miller's retirement at the Waste Management Phoenix Open on Friday, Feb. 1, 2019, at TPC Scottsdale in Scottsdale, Ariz. (IMAGN) 
 Hicks was also battling a pulmonary edema, which is the buildup of fluids in the lung, that came before an upper respiratory infection as well as autoimmune hemolytic anemia, The Post added according to the death certificate.
 Autoimmune hemolytic anemia is considered a rare condition where the immune system attacks red blood cells by mistake.
 SPORTS WORLD REACTS TO THE SUDDEN PASSING OF LEGENDARY BROADCASTER DAN HICKS AT THE AGE OF 64 
 Hannah Storm, the longtime ESPN broadcaster and wife of Hicks, announced her husband’s death Nov. 12 in a statement on X. She noted that it was an "acute illness" that led to his stunning passing.
 "Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness," Storm's statement began. "He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable.
 "Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around. When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered.
 Sports Journalists Hannah Storm (L) and Dan Hicks attend the 2023 Greenwich International Film Festival's Inspiration Talk & Award Ceremony at The Village on May 03, 2023 in Stamford, Connecticut. (Photo by Mark Sagliocco/Getty Images) (Mark Sagliocco/Getty Images) 
 "Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time. There are simply no words to express how much he will be missed."
 Hicks covered numerous sports during his illustrious broadcasting career, including Notre Dame Football, NBA and NFL. He was slated to call Notre Dame’s game against Boston College on Nov. 14.
 Tributes came pouring in around the globe, leading to many emotional moments including Al Michaels getting choked up speaking about Hicks on "Thursday Night Football" this past week.
 Dan Hicks attends U.S. Ski & Snowboard's 59th Annual Gold Medal Gala at The Ziegfeld Ballroom in New York City on Oct. 23, 2025. (Getty Images)
